name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Implement a shared, real-time dashboard that tracks the status of every pending video ID across all departments. Product Ops owns it. The trade-off is slower initial setup for faster, transparent coordination later.

name: Scriv
text: Reel’s dashboard risks becoming a stale artifact teams ignore if it lacks a built-in enforcement mechanism—like tying video IDs to active approvals in the AI Executive Assistant’s workflow. A better alternative: Product Ops enforces that no video ID moves to production without a timestamped entry in the dashboard, and the AI EA auto-flags stale entries weekly. That settles it: the dashboard is only useful if it’s the single source of truth, not just another spreadsheet.

name: Chisel
text:
Product Ops will build a single, real-time dashboard that locks every video ID to a live approval step in the AI Executive Assistant’s workflow. This forces every department to update the same source of truth before work moves forward, eliminating stale data and hidden bottlenecks. The trade-off is a short delay while Product Ops wires the approval hook into the existing assistant, but the payoff is one less meeting to chase status and one less surprise when a video stalls.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s dashboard locks approvals to the AI Executive Assistant’s workflow, but that risks overloading the Assistant with manual updates—turning it into a bottleneck instead of a coordinator. A better fix: Product Ops builds the dashboard but ties it to the existing approval triggers in the AI Creative Production workflow, letting the system auto-update while keeping enforcement. Settle it by testing the dashboard with one department for a week and measuring if approvals slow down.

name: Scope
text: Product Ops builds a single, real-time dashboard that locks every video ID to a live approval step in the AI Executive Assistant’s workflow. This forces every department to update the same source of truth before work moves forward, eliminating stale data and hidden bottlenecks. The trade-off is accepting a short-term slowdown in approvals while the Assistant learns to handle the new triggers—worth it for consistent, cross-department visibility.

name: Scriv
text: The risk is clear: locking the dashboard to the AI Executive Assistant’s workflow turns it into a single point of failure—if the Assistant stalls, *all* departments stall. Better: Product Ops builds the dashboard but ties it to the *existing* approval triggers in the AI Creative Production workflow, so updates flow automatically without manual overrides. Settle it by running a 48-hour pilot with one team to measure latency and error rates before scaling.
